sanskrit: śataṃ sahasrāṇi caturdaśeha; parā gatir jīvaguṇasya daitya ārohaṇaṃ tat kṛtam eva viddhi; sthānaṃ tathā niḥsaraṇaṃ ca teṣām
english: A hundred thousand and fourteen more, O Daitya — such is the supreme course of the soul's quality. Know that this is its ordained ascent, and likewise the stations and the final going-forth of those souls.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇasya varṇasya gatir nikṛṣṭā; sa majjate narake pacyamānaḥ sthānaṃ tathā durgatibhis tu tasya; prajāvisargān subahūn vadanti
english: Lowest is the course of the black color: such a soul sinks into hell and is cooked there. Its station, marked by evil destinies, the wise declare lasts through very many world-creations.

sanskrit: śataṃ sahasrāṇi tataś caritvā; prāpnoti varṇaṃ haritaṃ tu paścāt sa caiva tasmin nivasaty anīśo; yugakṣaye tamasā saṃvṛtātmā
english: Having wandered thereafter through a hundred thousand births, it at last attains the dusky color; yet still it dwells therein, without mastery of itself, its inner being wrapped in darkness at the closing of the age.

sanskrit: sa vai yadā sattvaguṇena yuktas; tamo vyapohan ghaṭate svabuddhyā sa lohitaṃ varṇam upaiti nīlo; manuṣyaloke parivartate ca
english: But when it is joined to the quality of sattva and, dispelling its darkness, strives by its own intelligence, then the blue-dusky soul comes to the red color and turns about within the world of men.

sanskrit: sa tatra saṃhāravisargam eva; svakarmajair bandhanaiḥ kliśyamānaḥ tataḥ sa hāridram upaiti varṇaṃ; saṃhāravikṣepaśate vyatīte
english: There, tormented by the bonds born of its own deeds, it passes through dissolution and emission; and when a hundred cycles of dissolution and dispersal have gone by, it comes thence to the yellow color.

sanskrit: hāridravarṇas tu prajāvisargān; sahasraśas tiṣṭhati saṃcaran vai avipramukto niraye ca daitya; tataḥ sahasrāṇi daśāparāṇi
english: Yet the yellow-colored soul abides, still roaming through thousands of world-emissions, not yet released from hell, O Daitya — for ten thousand further births beyond.

sanskrit: gatīḥ sahasrāṇi ca pañca tasya; catvāri saṃvartakṛtāni caiva vimuktam enaṃ nirayāc ca viddhi; sarveṣu cānyeṣu ca saṃbhaveṣu
english: Five thousand courses are its lot, and four more wrought by the world-dissolution; know that thereupon it is freed from hell, and from all other modes of becoming as well.

sanskrit: sa devaloke viharaty abhīkṣṇaṃ; tataś cyuto mānuṣatām upaiti saṃhāravikṣepaśatāni cāṣṭau; martyeṣu tiṣṭhann amṛtatvam eti
english: It disports itself again and again in the world of the gods; then, falling thence, it returns to the human state; and through eight hundred cycles of dissolution and dispersal, abiding among mortals, it attains to immortality.

sanskrit: so 'smād atha bhraśyati kālayogāt; kṛṣṇe tale tiṣṭhati sarvakaṣṭe yathā tv ayaṃ sidhyati jīvalokas; tat te 'bhidhāsyāmy asurapravīra
english: From this, in turn, it falls away by the working of time, and rests upon the black floor of all suffering. But how this world of living souls comes to perfection, that I shall declare to you, O foremost of Asuras.

sanskrit: daivāni sa vyūhaśatāni sapta; rakto haridro 'tha tathaiva śuklaḥ saṃśritya saṃdhāvati śuklam etam; aṣṭāparān arcyatamān sa lokān
english: Through seven hundred divine arrays, now red, now yellow, and now white, having taken its refuge it hastens toward that white state, and toward those eight further worlds most worthy of reverence.

sanskrit: aṣṭau ca ṣaṣṭiṃ ca śatāni yāni; manoviruddhāni mahādyutīnām śuklasya varṇasya parā gatir yā; trīṇy eva ruddhāni mahānubhāva
english: Of those eight hundred and sixty stations adverse to the mind, belonging to the mighty in splendor — the supreme course of the white color — only three remain barred, O greatly majestic one.

sanskrit: saṃhāravikṣepam aniṣṭam ekaṃ; catvāri cānyāni vasaty anīśaḥ ṣaṣṭhasya varṇasya parā gatir yā; siddhā viśiṣṭasya gataklamasya
english: One unwished dissolution-and-dispersal, and four others, it dwells in without mastery — such is the supreme course of the sixth color, perfected, distinguished, its weariness gone.

sanskrit: saptottaraṃ teṣu vasaty anīśaḥ; saṃhāravikṣepaśataṃ saśeṣam tasmād upāvṛtya manuṣyaloke; tato mahān mānuṣatām upaiti
english: For a hundred and seven cycles of dissolution and dispersal, still with a remainder, it dwells there without mastery; then, turning back into the world of men, the great soul attains anew to human birth.

sanskrit: tasmād upāvṛtya tataḥ krameṇa; so 'gre sma saṃtiṣṭhati bhūtasargam sa saptakṛtvaś ca paraiti lokān; saṃhāravikṣepakṛtapravāsaḥ
english: Turning back from that, then by degrees it comes at last to stand at the head of the creation of beings; and seven times over it passes beyond the worlds, having made its sojourn through dissolution and dispersal.

sanskrit: saptaiva saṃhāram upaplavāni; saṃbhāvya saṃtiṣṭhati siddhaloke tato 'vyayaṃ sthānam anantam eti; devasya viṣṇor atha brahmaṇaś ca śeṣasya caivātha narasya caiva; devasya viṣṇoḥ paramasya caiva
english: Having undergone seven dissolutions and floods, it comes to rest in the world of the perfected; then it goes to the imperishable, infinite station — of the god Viṣṇu, and of Brahmā, and of Śeṣa, and of Nara, yea, of the supreme god Viṣṇu himself.

sanskrit: saṃhārakāle paridagdhakāyā; brahmāṇam āyānti sadā prajā hi ceṣṭātmano devagaṇāś ca sarve; ye brahmalokād amarāḥ sma te 'pi
english: At the time of dissolution, their bodies wholly consumed, the creatures always pass into Brahmā; and the active-natured hosts of gods as well — even those immortals who are of Brahmā's world.

sanskrit: prajāvisargaṃ tu saśeṣakālaṃ; sthānāni svāny eva saranti jīvāḥ niḥśeṣāṇāṃ tat padaṃ yānti cānte; sarvāpadā ye sadṛśā manuṣyāḥ
english: But through the creation of beings, while a portion of time remains, the souls move on to their own proper stations; and at the end the souls that have no remnant left reach that abode — the men who are alike in having passed beyond all calamities.

sanskrit: ye tu cyutāḥ siddhalokāt krameṇa; teṣāṃ gatiṃ yānti tathānupūrvyā jīvāḥ pare tadbalaveṣarūpā; vidhiṃ svakaṃ yānti viparyayeṇa
english: But those souls who have fallen by stages from the world of the perfected go to their course in due succession; while the others, taking on the strength, garb, and form of that state, attain their own ordained lot by the reverse order.

sanskrit: sa yāvad evāsti saśeṣabhukte; prajāś ca devyau ca tathaiva śukle tāvat tadā teṣu viśuddhabhāvaḥ; saṃyamya pañcendriyarūpam etat
english: So long as there abides a remnant yet to be enjoyed — the creatures, the two goddesses, and likewise the white state — so long does the soul of purified being remain among them, restraining this fivefold form of the senses.

sanskrit: śuddhāṃ gatiṃ tāṃ paramāṃ paraiti; śuddhena nityaṃ manasā vicinvan tato 'vyayaṃ sthānam upaiti brahma; duṣprāpam abhyeti sa śāśvataṃ vai ity etad ākhyātam ahīnasattva; nārāyaṇasyeha balaṃ mayā te
english: It reaches that supreme, pure course, ever meditating with a purified mind; then it attains the imperishable station of Brahman, and comes to that eternal goal so hard to win. Thus, O you of undiminished being, the power of Nārāyaṇa has been declared to you by me.

sanskrit: vṛtra uvāca evaṃ gate me na viṣādo 'sti kaś cit; samyak ca paśyāmi vacas tavaitat śrutvā ca te vācam adīnasattva; vikalmaṣo 'smy adya tathā vipāpmā
english: Vṛtra said: With matters thus, no grief remains in me at all, and I rightly perceive this teaching of yours; and having heard your word, O you of undejected spirit, I am this day cleansed of taint and freed from sin.

sanskrit: pravṛttam etad bhagavan maharṣe; mahādyuteś cakram anantavīryam viṣṇor anantasya sanātanaṃ tat; sthānaṃ sargā yatra sarve pravṛttāḥ sa vai mahātmā puruṣottamo vai; tasmiñ jagat sarvam idaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
english: This wheel of the mighty-splendored one is set in motion, O blessed great seer, of boundless might — that eternal station of infinite Viṣṇu, wherein all creations have their origin. He indeed is the great soul, the supreme Person; in him this whole universe is established.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktvā sa kaunteya vṛtraḥ prāṇān avāsṛjat yojayitvā tathātmānaṃ paraṃ sthānam avāptavān
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus, O son of Kuntī, Vṛtra gave up his life-breaths; and yoking his self thereby, he attained the supreme station.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ayaṃ sa bhagavān devaḥ pitāmaha janārdanaḥ sanatkumāro vṛtrāya yat tad ākhyātavān purā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Is this, O grandsire, that same blessed god Janārdana, whom of old Sanatkumāra declared to Vṛtra?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca mūlasthāyī sa bhagavān svenānantena tejasā tatsthaḥ sṛjati tān bhāvān nānārūpān mahātapāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: That blessed one, abiding at the root, by his own infinite radiance — stationed therein, the great ascetic creates those beings in their manifold forms.

sanskrit: turīyārdhena tasyemaṃ viddhi keśavam acyutam turīyārdhena lokāṃs trīn bhāvayaty eṣa buddhimān
english: Know this Keśava, the unfallen, to be of one half of his fourth part; with that half of a fourth this wise one sustains the three worlds.

sanskrit: arvāk sthitas tu yaḥ sthāyī kalpānte parivartate sa śete bhagavān apsu yo 'sāv atibalaḥ prabhuḥ tān vidhātā prasannātmā lokāṃś carati śāśvatān
english: But he who abides on the nearer side, enduring, turns about at the end of the aeon; that blessed lord of surpassing might lies upon the waters; and the Ordainer, serene of soul, ranges through those eternal worlds.

sanskrit: sarvāṇy aśūnyāni karoty anantaḥ; sanatkumāraḥ saṃcarate ca lokān sa cāniruddhaḥ sṛjate mahātmā; tatsthaṃ jagat sarvam idaṃ vicitram
english: The Infinite makes all things unempty, and as Sanatkumāra he wanders through the worlds; and as Aniruddha that great soul brings forth creation — in him stands this whole variegated universe.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vṛtreṇa paramārthajña dṛṣṭā manye ''tmano gatiḥ śubhā tasmāt sa sukhito na śocati pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I think, O knower of the highest truth, that Vṛtra beheld the blessed course of his own self; therefore he was happy and grieved not, O grandsire.

sanskrit: śuklaḥ śuklābhijātīyaḥ sādhyo nāvartate 'nagha tiryaggateś ca nirmukto nirayāc ca pitāmaha
english: The white one, of white birth and ripe for accomplishment, returns no more, O sinless one; he is released both from the course of the brute creatures and from hell, O grandsire.

sanskrit: hāridravarṇe rakte vā vartamānas tu pārthiva tiryag evānupaśyeta karmabhis tāmasair vṛtaḥ
english: But one who dwells in the yellow color or the red, O king, beholds before him only the brute estate, hemmed in by deeds born of darkness.

sanskrit: vayaṃ tu bhṛśam āpannā raktāḥ kaṣṭamukhe 'sukhe kāṃ gatiṃ pratipatsyāmo nīlāṃ kṛṣṇādhamām atha
english: But we, sorely fallen, red of color, set in the face of hardship and joylessness — what course shall we attain? The blue, or else the black, lowest of all?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śuddhābhijanasaṃpannāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ vihṛtya devalokeṣu punar mānuṣyam eṣyatha
english: Bhīṣma said: O Pāṇḍavas, endowed with pure lineage and firm in your vows, having disported yourselves in the worlds of the gods, you shall come again to the human state.

sanskrit: prajāvisargaṃ ca sukhena kāle; pratyetya deveṣu sukhāni bhuktvā sukhena saṃyāsyatha siddhasaṃkhyāṃ; mā vo bhayaṃ bhūd vimalāḥ stha sarve
english: And in due time, in happiness, returning through the creation of beings, having enjoyed delights among the gods, you shall pass in happiness into the number of the perfected. Let there be no fear for you — stainless are you all.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca aho dharmiṣṭhatā tāta vṛtrasyāmitatejasaḥ yasya vijñānam atulaṃ viṣṇor bhaktiś ca tādṛśī
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How great, O father, was the righteousness of Vṛtra of immeasurable splendor, whose discernment was beyond compare and whose devotion to Viṣṇu was such as this!

sanskrit: durvijñeyam idaṃ tāta viṣṇor amitatejasaḥ kathaṃ vā rājaśārdūla padaṃ taj jñātavān asau
english: Hard to be known is this, O father — the station of Viṣṇu of immeasurable splendor; how then, O tiger among kings, did he come to know that abode?

sanskrit: bhavatā kathitaṃ hy etac chraddadhe cāham acyuta bhūyas tu me samutpannā buddhir avyaktadarśanāt
english: This has been told by you, and I believe it, O unfaltering one; yet a further thought has arisen in me from this glimpse of the Unmanifest.

sanskrit: kathaṃ vinihato vṛtraḥ śakreṇa bharatarṣabha dharmiṣṭho viṣṇubhaktaś ca tattvajñaś ca padānvaye
english: How was Vṛtra slain by Śakra, O bull of the Bharatas — he so righteous, so devoted to Viṣṇu, and so versed in the truth of that abode's order?

sanskrit: etan me saṃśayaṃ brūhi pṛcchato bharatarṣabha vṛtras tu rājaśārdūla yathā śakreṇa nirjitaḥ
english: Resolve this doubt of mine, who ask it, O bull of the Bharatas — how Vṛtra was vanquished by Śakra, O tiger among kings.

sanskrit: yathā caivābhavad yuddhaṃ tac cācakṣva pitāmaha vistareṇa mahābāho paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: And tell me too how the battle came to be, O grandsire, in full detail, O mighty-armed one; for great is my curiosity.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rathenendraḥ prayāto vai sārdhaṃ suragaṇaiḥ purā dadarśāthāgrato vṛtraṃ viṣṭhitaṃ parvatopamam
english: Bhīṣma said: Indra, having set forth of old upon his chariot together with the hosts of the gods, beheld before him Vṛtra standing like a mountain.

sanskrit: yojanānāṃ śatāny ūrdhvaṃ pañcocchritam ariṃdama śatāni vistareṇātha trīṇy evābhyadhikāni tu
english: Five hundred leagues he rose in height, O subduer of foes, and three hundred and more across in breadth.

sanskrit: tat prekṣya tādṛśaṃ rūpaṃ trailokyenāpi durjayam vṛtrasya devāḥ saṃtrastā na śāntim upalebhire
english: Beholding that form of Vṛtra, so vast, unconquerable even by the three worlds, the gods were stricken with terror and could find no peace.

sanskrit: śakrasya tu tadā rājann ūrustambho vyajāyata bhayād vṛtrasya sahasā dṛṣṭvā tad rūpam uttamam
english: And then, O king, a numbness of the thighs came over Śakra, out of fear of Vṛtra, when of a sudden he saw that surpassing form.

sanskrit: tato nādaḥ samabhavad vāditrāṇāṃ ca nisvanaḥ devāsurāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ tasmin yuddha upasthite
english: Then arose a clamor and the din of instruments among all the gods and Asuras, as that battle drew on.

sanskrit: atha vṛtrasya kauravya dṛṣṭvā śakram upasthitam na saṃbhramo na bhīḥ kā cid āsthā vā samajāyata
english: But in Vṛtra, O Kaurava, when he saw Śakra come near, there arose neither agitation, nor any fear, nor any care.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ trailokyasya bhayaṃkaram śakrasya ca surendrasya vṛtrasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Then began a battle terrifying to the three worlds, between Śakra, lord of the gods, and the great-souled Vṛtra.

sanskrit: asibhiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ śūlaiḥ śaktitomaramudgaraiḥ śilābhir vividhābhiś ca kārmukaiś ca mahāsvanaiḥ
english: With swords and spiked maces, with pikes, with lances, javelins, and hammers, with rocks of every kind, and with loud-twanging bows;

sanskrit: astraiś ca vividhair divyaiḥ pāvakolkābhir eva ca devāsurais tataḥ sainyaiḥ sarvam āsīt samākulam
english: and with manifold celestial weapons, and with firebrands of flame — by the armies of gods and Asuras all the world was then thrown into tumult.

sanskrit: pitāmahapurogāś ca sarve devagaṇās tathā ṛṣayaś ca mahābhāgās tad yuddhaṃ draṣṭum āgaman
english: And all the hosts of the gods, with the Grandsire at their head, and the greatly blessed seers, came to behold that battle.

sanskrit: vimānāgryair mahārāja siddhāś ca bharatarṣabha gandharvāś ca vimānāgryair apsarobhiḥ samāgaman
english: In their finest sky-chariots, O great king, the Siddhas, O bull of the Bharatas, and the Gandharvas in their finest chariots, came together with the Apsarases.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣam āvṛtya vṛtro dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ aśmavarṣeṇa devendraṃ parvatāt samavākirat
english: Then Vṛtra, foremost of the upholders of righteousness, overspreading the firmament, showered down upon Indra a rain of stones from the mountain.

sanskrit: tato devagaṇāḥ kruddhāḥ sarvataḥ śastravṛṣṭibhiḥ aśmavarṣam apohanta vṛtrapreritam āhave
english: Then the hosts of the gods, enraged, with showers of weapons from every side, drove off that rain of stones that Vṛtra had sent forth in the battle.

sanskrit: vṛtraś ca kuruśārdūla mahāmāyo mahābalaḥ mohayām āsa devendraṃ māyāyuddhena sarvataḥ
english: And Vṛtra, O tiger of the Kurus, master of great illusion and great might, bewildered Indra on every side by a warfare of magic.

sanskrit: tasya vṛtrārditasyātha moha āsīc chatakratoḥ rathaṃtareṇa taṃ tatra vasiṣṭhaḥ samabodhayat
english: Then a stupor fell upon Śatakratu, sore beset by Vṛtra; and Vasiṣṭha there roused him with the Rathaṃtara hymn.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca devaśreṣṭho 'si devendra surārivinibarhaṇa trailokyabalasaṃyuktaḥ kasmāc chakra viṣīdasi
english: Vasiṣṭha said: You are the best of the gods, O Indra, crusher of the foes of the gods, endowed with the strength of the three worlds — why, O Śakra, do you despond?

sanskrit: eṣa brahmā ca viṣṇuś ca śivaś caiva jagatprabhuḥ somaś ca bhagavān devaḥ sarve ca paramarṣayaḥ
english: Here are Brahmā and Viṣṇu, and Śiva the lord of the world, and the blessed god Soma, and all the supreme seers.

sanskrit: mā kārṣīḥ kaśmalaṃ śakra kaś cid evetaro yathā āryāṃ yuddhe matiṃ kṛtvā jahi śatruṃ sureśvara
english: Give not way to faintness, O Śakra, like some lesser one; setting a noble resolve upon the fight, slay your foe, O lord of the gods.

sanskrit: eṣa lokagurus tryakṣaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ nirīkṣate tvāṃ bhagavāṃs tyaja mohaṃ sureśvara
english: Here the three-eyed teacher of the world, revered by all the worlds, the blessed one, looks upon you; cast off your bewilderment, O lord of the gods.

sanskrit: ete brahmarṣayaś caiva bṛhaspatipurogamāḥ stavena śakra divyena stuvanti tvāṃ jayāya vai
english: And these Brahman-seers, with Bṛhaspati at their head, praise you, O Śakra, with a celestial hymn of praise, that you may have the victory.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evaṃ saṃbodhyamānasya vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā atīva vāsavasyāsīd balam uttamatejasaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: As he was thus roused by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, the strength of Vāsava, supreme in splendor, grew exceedingly.

sanskrit: tato buddhim upāgamya bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ yogena mahatā yuktas tāṃ māyāṃ vyapakarṣata
english: Then the blessed chastiser of Pāka, recovering his wits and joined to a mighty yoga, drew off that illusion.

sanskrit: tato 'ṅgiraḥsutaḥ śrīmāṃs te caiva paramarṣayaḥ dṛṣṭvā vṛtrasya vikrāntam upagamya maheśvaram ūcur vṛtravināśārthaṃ lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: Then the glorious son of Aṅgiras, and those supreme seers, seeing the prowess of Vṛtra, drew near to Maheśvara and spoke, for the destruction of Vṛtra and out of desire for the welfare of the worlds:

sanskrit: tato bhagavatas tejo jvaro bhūtvā jagatpateḥ samāviśan mahāraudraṃ vṛtraṃ daityavaraṃ tadā
english: Then the radiance of the blessed lord of the world, becoming a fever, entered into that most dreadful Vṛtra, the foremost of the Daityas.

sanskrit: viṣṇuś ca bhagavān devaḥ sarvalokābhipūjitaḥ aindraṃ samāviśad vajraṃ lokasaṃrakṣaṇe rataḥ
english: And the blessed god Viṣṇu, worshipped by all the worlds, intent upon the protection of the worlds, entered into Indra's thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tato bṛhaspatir dhīmān upāgamya śatakratum vasiṣṭhaś ca mahātejāḥ sarve ca paramarṣayaḥ
english: Then wise Bṛhaspati, drawing near to Śatakratu, and Vasiṣṭha of great splendor, and all the supreme seers —

sanskrit: te samāsādya varadaṃ vāsavaṃ lokapūjitam ūcur ekāgramanaso jahi vṛtram iti prabho
english: approaching the boon-giving Vāsava, honored by the worlds, they said with single-minded purpose: "Slay Vṛtra, O lord!"

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca eṣa vṛtro mahāñ śakra balena mahatā vṛtaḥ viśvātmā sarvagaś caiva bahumāyaś ca viśrutaḥ
english: Maheśvara said: This Vṛtra is mighty, O Śakra, girt about with great strength, soul of the universe, all-pervading, and renowned as a master of many illusions.

sanskrit: tad enam asuraśreṣṭhaṃ trailokyenāpi durjayam jahi tvaṃ yogam āsthāya māvamaṃsthāḥ sureśvara
english: Therefore slay this best of Asuras, unconquerable even by the three worlds, taking your stand upon yoga; despise him not, O lord of the gods.

sanskrit: anena hi tapas taptaṃ balārtham amarādhipa ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣasahasrāṇi brahmā cāsmai varaṃ dadau
english: For by him austerity was practiced for the sake of strength, O sovereign of the immortals, for sixty thousand years; and Brahmā granted him a boon —

sanskrit: mahattvaṃ yogināṃ caiva mahāmāyatvam eva ca mahābalatvaṃ ca tathā tejaś cāgryaṃ sureśvara
english: the greatness of yogins, and mastery of great illusion, and great might, and foremost splendor besides, O lord of the gods.

sanskrit: etad vai māmakaṃ tejaḥ samāviśati vāsava vṛtram enaṃ tvam apy evaṃ jahi vajreṇa dānavam
english: Lo, this radiance of mine enters into him, O Vāsava; do you in like manner slay this Vṛtra, this Dānava, with your thunderbolt.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca bhagavaṃs tvatprasādena ditijaṃ sudurāsadam vajreṇa nihaniṣyāmi paśyatas te surarṣabha
english: Śakra said: O blessed one, by your grace I shall slay with my thunderbolt this son of Diti, so hard to assail, while you look on, O bull of the gods.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca āviśyamāne daitye tu jvareṇātha mahāsure devatānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca harṣān nādo mahān abhūt
english: Bhīṣma said: As the fever entered into that Daitya, the great Asura, there arose a mighty clamor of joy from the gods and the seers.

sanskrit: tato dundubhayaś caiva śaṅkhāś ca sumahāsvanāḥ murajā ḍiṇḍimāś caiva prāvādyanta sahasraśaḥ
english: Then kettledrums and conches of mighty sound, and tabors and tambourines, were sounded by the thousand.

sanskrit: asurāṇāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ smṛtilopo 'bhavan mahān prajñānāśaś ca balavān kṣaṇena samapadyata
english: But upon all the Asuras there came a great loss of memory, and in an instant a powerful failing of their understanding overtook them.

sanskrit: tam āviṣṭam atho jñātvā ṛṣayo devatās tathā stuvantaḥ śakram īśānaṃ tathā prācodayann api
english: Then, knowing him to be thus possessed, the seers and the gods, praising Śakra the lord, urged him on as well.

sanskrit: rathasthasya hi śakrasya yuddhakāle mahātmanaḥ ṛṣibhiḥ stūyamānasya rūpam āsīt sudurdṛśam
english: For as the great-souled Śakra stood upon his chariot in the hour of battle, praised by the seers, his form was very hard to look upon.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vṛtrasya tu mahārāja jvarāviṣṭasya sarvaśaḥ abhavan yāni liṅgāni śarīre tāni me śṛṇu
english: Bhīṣma said: But of Vṛtra, O great king, wholly possessed by the fever, hear from me the signs that appeared upon his body.

sanskrit: jvalitāsyo 'bhavad ghoro vaivarṇyaṃ cāgamat param gātrakampaś ca sumahāñ śvāsaś cāpy abhavan mahān romaharṣaś ca tīvro 'bhūn niḥśvāsaś ca mahān nṛpa
english: His mouth grew flaming and dreadful, and an extreme pallor came over him; a violent trembling of the limbs and a heavy panting seized him; a fierce bristling of the hair arose, and his breathing came hard, O king.
